subject: Multi-year commitment & true-up mechanics — proposal and buffer-band clarifications
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amelia Park <amelia.park@titanhealth.com>, procurement@titanhealth.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Multi-year commitment + true-up buffer — preliminary proposal

Hi Amelia / Titan procurement team,

Thanks for taking the time last week. Per our conversation, attached is a preliminary outline for a multi-year prepay structure that aims to balance predictability for TitanHealth with built-in flexibility for ramping usage. High-level highlights: 

- Term: 3 years, annual prepay buckets (paid in year 1 for years 1–3).
- Discounting: step-down discounts tied to committed annual spend tiers (higher commit -> additional 7.5% effective discount on unit price, see proposal).
- Ramp schedule: Year 1 baseline + staged ramp (we've modeled a conservative 25% YoY growth default).
- True-up / overage mechanics: annual reconciliation at each contract-year end. If actual usage > prepaid units beyond the buffer band, overage billed at list minus negotiated overage discount; if usage < prepaid by more than the buffer band, remaining credits may (a) roll forward to next year up to a carry cap or (b) be refunded at a reduced rate (see options).
- Buffer band: we propose a +/-10% buffer on annual usage to avoid frequent true-ups for small variances.

I'm attaching the first-draft proposal (Titan_MultiYear_Proposal_v1.pdf) and an initial ramp schedule spreadsheet (Titan_Ramp_Schedule.xlsx) so your finance team can run the numbers. 

Questions for your team:
1) Would Titan prefer unused credits to roll forward (with a cap) or be credited/refunded at the end of the year?
2) Is a +/-10% buffer band acceptable, or do you want a wider initial band for year 1?
3) For overage pricing, do you need a hard cap on per-token overage spend?

If it helps, happy to sync this week for 30 minutes with legal and finance to walk through the example math.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: Titan_MultiYear_Proposal_v1.pdf (pdf), Titan_Ramp_Schedule.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Amelia Park <amelia.park@titanhealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@titanhealth.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 12:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-year commitment + true-up buffer — preliminary proposal

Thanks Vanessa — appreciate the detailed starter. A few items finance/legal want clarified before we schedule a call: 

1) End-of-term reconciliation: clarify whether unused prepaid units after year 3 expire with zero value, or whether Titan can request a pro rata refund for remaining credits. Our CFO prefers a refund option for material underruns.

2) Buffer bands: +/-10% seems tight given our pilot uncertainty. Can you outline a first-year wider band (eg, +/-20%) that tightens in later years?

3) Overages: we need to understand how overage pricing differs from the committed unit price. Please show an explicit per-token example (annual usage 6.5M vs prepaid 5M with a 15% buffer).

4) Ramp increases: if we exceed committed growth and move into a higher tier mid-year, do we get retroactive price tiering or only at next reconciliation?

Please loop in whoever owns the contract language on refunds and carry-forward caps. If you can send an updated proposal reflecting the two buffer band options and an example calculation, that would help.

Regards,
Amelia Park
CFO | TitanHealth
amelia.park@titanhealth.com
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Multi-year commitment + true-up buffer — preliminary proposal (Titan request)

Folks — forwarding Titan's clarification requests. Key asks: refund option at EOT for material underruns, wider first-year buffer possibility, explicit overage math, and whether mid-year tier increases can be retroactive.

My suggested negotiation posture:
- Offer two paths: (A) Carry-forward up to 25% of unused credits year-over-year (no cash refund), or (B) end-of-term pro rata refund capped at 20% of prepay value (refund at 50% of MSRP for remaining capacity). Option A protects our revenue predictability; B gives Titan CFO a refund runway.
- Buffer: propose +/-20% year 1, tightening to +/-10% year 2+, which addresses their pilot uncertainty.
- Overage: bill overage at list price minus 5% (explicit example in spreadsheet). Allow retroactive tier re-price at annual true-up only (not mid-year), but include a clause for discretionary crediting if they sustain a sustained higher usage and agree to amend commit.

Rishi — can you run margin impact for the two options (A / B) and confirm net revenue sensitivity?
Marissa — can you prepare an updated proposal and attach a clean example calculation table for Amelia (show 5M prepaid, 6.5M actual, buffer at 15%/20%).
Karthik — legal/finance: please flag any compliance or accounting concerns with an end-of-term refund clause (cap/refund rate).

Thanks — I'd like to send an updated proposal tomorrow.

— Vanessa
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amelia Park <amelia.park@titanhealth.com>, procurement@titanhealth.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Multi-year commitment + true-up buffer — preliminary proposal (updated)

Hi Amelia — thanks for the quick feedback. Attached are two options (Proposal_v2) plus a worked example. Summary of the updates per your questions: 

1) End-of-term reconciliation: two options presented: 
  - Option A (Preferred by Redwood): carry-forward up to 25% of unused prepaid units year-over-year; unused units beyond 25% expire at contract year end. No cash refunds.
  - Option B: end-of-term pro rata refund for remaining prepaid units capped at 20% of the annual prepay value; refunds executed at 50% of the current list price to account for reserved capacity and amortized discounts.

2) Buffer bands: we propose +/-20% for Year 1, +/-10% for Years 2–3. If you prefer a steady band we can do +/-15% across all years.

3) Overage pricing example: Prepaid = 5,000,000 units; Actual = 6,500,000 units; Buffer = 15% (750k) → chargeable overage = 6.5M - (5M + 0.75M) = 750k units. Overage rate = list rate * 0.95 (5% discount on list). Example math attached in pricing_options_for_Titan.xlsx.

4) Tier movement: price tier changes are applied at annual true-up. For mid-year sustained increases we can add a discretionary amendment path: if quarterly run-rate exceeds the next tier for two consecutive quarters, we will support a mid-term amendment with retroactive crediting limited to the quarter in which the amendment was signed. 

Next steps: if Option A (carry-forward) is acceptable, that preserves our revenue profile and gives Titan runway to ramp. If Titan wants Option B, there will be a modest increase in base unit price to offset refund exposure (shown in the proposal).

Would you be available for a 30-minute call tomorrow or Friday with finance/legal to lock the path? I'll send a calendar invite once I hear preferred times.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Titan_MultiYear_Proposal_v2.pdf (pdf), Titan_Ramp_Schedule.xlsx (xlsx), pricing_options_for_Titan.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Amelia Park <amelia.park@titanhealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@titanhealth.com
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-year commitment + true-up buffer — preliminary proposal (updated)

Vanessa — thanks for the clear options and the worked example. Titan's CFO team is inclined toward Option A (carry-forward up to 25% year-over-year) combined with a Year 1 buffer at +/-20% that tightens to +/-10% thereafter. The team also prefers the annual true-up approach with the discretionary mid-term amendment language you proposed.

Next steps: please send a 30-minute invite including your legal and finance folks. Procurement will want a short clause in the contract defining the carry cap and the refund avoidance language. We'll have our legal counsel draft redlines after your initial contract arrives. Also please include a DocuSign-ready version of the proposal once the final option is chosen.

Times that work for our team: Fri 11:00–12:30 PT or Mon 14:00–16:00 PT.

I'll expect your calendar invite.

Best,
Amelia Park
CFO | TitanHealth
